exercises.title: Electrical Safety and the Electronics Workflow: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: You are powering an unknown 12 V board for the first time from a bench supply. Which setup is safest?
choices: Output at 0 V, current limit around 100 mA, polarity verified with the output off, then raise the voltage while watching current
Set 12 V and a 5 A limit so the board never trips the supply during start-up
Clip the scope ground to the board's return to watch the rails, since a grounded clip is harmless
Power it directly and check polarity afterwards from any smoke or heat
hints: Limit the energy available before you know the board is healthy.

exercises.title: Electrical Safety and the Electronics Workflow: worked analysis
exercises.instructionMarkdown:
A 12 V bench supply limited to 100 mA feeds an unknown board. Establish a safe current limit, inspect polarity, and document the power-up sequence.

Show assumptions, equations, units, standard-value choices, ratings, tolerance effects, and the measurements that would verify the result.
checklist: I drew or described the complete source and return path.
I carried units and checked the order of magnitude.
I checked ratings and at least one worst-case condition.
I wrote an observable verification step before viewing the solution.
hints: Start with a symbolic relationship before substituting numbers.
Separate typical behavior from guaranteed limits and add measurement tolerance.
exercises.solutionMarkdown:
## Reference solution

Use a 12 V extra-low-voltage source, set the output to 0 V before connection, set a 100 mA current limit, verify lead polarity with the output disabled, inspect for shorts, then raise voltage while watching current. Stop on current limit, heating, odor, or an unexpected rail. Record the discharged-state resistance only after confirming capacitors are safe.

The governing principle is: **separate SELV work from mains and high-energy battery work; identify shock, burn, fire, stored-energy, and probe-ground hazards**. Define every reference direction and convert values to coherent SI units. Compare the result with component ratings and standard available values, then report a bounded expectation that includes tolerance, temperature, supply variation, and instrument loading.

### Verification evidence

1. Power off and confirm wiring, polarity, and discharge state.
2. Configure a conservative current limit.
3. Predict source current and the critical node voltages or waveform features.
4. Power on and compare the first measurement with the bounded prediction.
5. Stop if current, temperature, smell, or waveform exceeds the safe bound.

The notebook should make both the reasoning and bench test independently reproducible.

exercises.title: Electrical Safety and the Electronics Workflow: measurement and fault investigation
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Plan or perform a low-voltage investigation of **unsafe ground clip, reversed polarity, missing current limit, charged capacitor**. Record a safe setup, predicted healthy evidence, observed evidence, one hypothesis at a time, and the final verification.
checklist: I documented the de-energized inspection and safe current limit.
I recorded expected healthy readings before measuring.
I used one falsifiable hypothesis at a time.
I included final evidence that distinguishes cause from symptom.
hints: Measure the supply current and block boundaries before probing internal details.
Change only one condition between measurements.
